question: How does First American account for title insurance loss reserves?
expected_answer: Losses are provided for by a charge to expense when the related premium revenue is recognised, determined by applying a loss provision rate to total title insurance premiums and escrow fees. Management sets the rate at the start of each year and reassesses it quarterly, informed by an in-house actuarial review, so that the known claims and IBNR reserves together reflect its best estimate of the total cost to settle all claims; an adjustment is recorded if the ending IBNR reserve is not adequate.

question: How does First American describe the role of its title plants?
expected_answer: Title plants are described as one of the company's principal assets. They hold information abstracted from public records but arrange it geographically rather than by the names of the parties to a document, which is how public records are indexed, so title searches can be run more efficiently. Many title plants also index prior title insurance policies, adding further searching efficiency, and they support operations beyond title insurance.

question: What does First American disclose about its escrow deposits and trust assets?
